chapters.label: Intro
chapters.text: Good morning. It's Saturday, November 28th, the Spurs won, UTSA won, and the weather is behaving. Let's get into it.

chapters.label: 🌤️ Weather
chapters.text: Dress in layers today. It starts chilly at 42, feels more like 36 with the wind, then climbs to a high of 73. Midday is 65, the afternoon is 72, and it's back down to 59 by evening. Zero chance of rain. Sunday through Tuesday is cloudy and dry, then drizzle shows up Wednesday and sticks around Thursday with a 43 percent chance.

chapters.label: 🏆 My Teams
chapters.text: The Spurs beat the Lakers 99 to 96 and are now 16 and 4. They were down by 20 and came all the way back. Stephon Castle had 26 points and 9 assists, and the win sends San Antonio into the NBA Cup knockout round as a wild card. Not a bad way to spend a Friday.

chapters.label: 🏆 My Teams
chapters.text: UTSA took care of Tulsa, 28 to 22, and moves to 10 and 2. AJ Wilson did most of the damage with four catches for 153 yards and two touchdowns. That's an average of nearly 38 yards a catch, if you like doing math on a Saturday. The win also locks up home field for the American Conference title game, so the Roadrunners get to host it.

chapters.label: 🏈 Sports
chapters.text: The Lakers, meanwhile, had a rough night in San Antonio, and Luka Dončić took it personally. He went 1 for 13 from three in the loss. Over the last couple of weeks he's 26 for 100. After the game he flung his wristband toward a woman in the crowd, then turned around to retrieve it. The man with her handed it back and shoved him, and security stepped in fast. Luka says he throws his wristband almost every game, heard she didn't want it, and went back to get it. The video shows the woman saying something first, and he appeared to flip a middle finger earlier. So his wristband found its target more reliably than his jumper did. Meanwhile, the Spurs fans just watched a 20-point lead evaporate on the other side, and that's the part we're enjoying.

chapters.label: 🇺🇸 U.S.
chapters.text: Thanksgiving did not go well on the East Coast. A powerful storm swept through from New York to Virginia, flooding streets, knocking down trees and power lines, and cutting power to nearly a million customers at its peak. More than 260,000 were still in the dark on Friday. It was the wettest Thanksgiving on record in Washington, and nearly two inches fell in New York's Central Park. Hundreds of flights were canceled both days, and one traveler sat in LaGuardia for thirteen hours trying to get to Chicago. Several states declared emergencies, and the president says he'll consider releasing emergency funds. Skies cleared Friday, and crews are working through the repairs.

chapters.label: 🇺🇸 U.S.
chapters.text: The one tradition that actually got canceled by that storm gets a do-over today. Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade, postponed for the first time ever, is stepping off this morning with all the balloons, floats and a thousand clowns. Some marching bands from out of town had to scramble to raise tens or even hundreds of thousands of dollars to stay in New York a few extra days. The celebrity lineup mostly survives, and they've added Gloria Gaynor and LL Cool J. Yes, the I Will Survive woman for the parade that just survived. NBC and Peacock have it from 8:30 Eastern, so 7:30 here, until noon Eastern. The National Dog Show rebroadcast follows.

chapters.label: 🇺🇸 U.S.
chapters.text: Apple sued OpenAI in June, accusing it of stealing trade secrets to build hardware, naming OpenAI's chief hardware officer Tang Tan and a technical staffer, Chang Liu. Both used to work at Apple. On Friday OpenAI hit back with a countersuit, saying Apple deliberately sets up departing employees so it can accuse them, and their new employers, of stealing whenever convenient. It calls that a trap. Apple says that's a distraction and notes OpenAI has already been ordered to stop using Apple's confidential information. The backdrop is that OpenAI bought the device startup of Jony Ive, the designer behind the iPhone, last year. So Apple's old design star is now building the thing Apple is suing over, and no one is surprised the lawyers got involved.

chapters.label: 💻 Tech
chapters.text: Court filings are filling in how the government ended up owning ten percent of Intel. In August 2025, a Commerce Department lawyer told Intel's chief financial officer not to make the mistake of thinking this was a negotiation. The board could say no, he said, but there would be consequences he couldn't predict. Days later, the board said yes. Trump announced the government now owned ten percent, valued around eleven billion dollars, for which the United States paid nothing. Very bold approach to the old line, nice chip company you've got there, shame if something happened to it. It also fits a pattern. Trump said this week he convinced Nvidia's board to rehire chief executive Jensen Huang.

chapters.label: 🎬 Culture & Entertainment
chapters.text: Carly Rae Jepsen has spent a decade being told her best song isn't Call Me Maybe, and fans have always agreed. It's Run Away With Me, released in 2015, and it stalled at number 58 on the charts. Then it turned up in Grand Theft Auto VI, soundtracking a sequence with jet skis and champagne bottles shot off the back of a yacht. Its daily streams went from 20,000 to 281,000 overnight, and it just landed at a new UK peak of 28. Jepsen says she hasn't played the game yet and plans to become a late-in-life gamer. A song about falling head over heels with someone, now with explosions nearby. Seems about right.

chapters.label: ⚡ Quick hits
chapters.text: A few quick ones. A truck crashed into a San Antonio dog daycare on Thanksgiving, and one dog is still missing. Canada's Supreme Court voted six to one to largely uphold Quebec's ban on religious symbols for public sector workers, and critics say it guts minority rights. Customs officers in Amsterdam found 26 Vallarta mud turtles, some of the rarest in the world, duct-taped inside a traveler's checked bag, and an arrest was made. The mall is not dead: indoor mall visits rose four percent last month, outdoor ones almost six, and teens have rediscovered hanging out. And in Britain, online pension and benefits services are still down after what the government calls a cyber incident, though payments are supposed to continue.

chapters.label: Wrapping up
chapters.text: That's your Saturday. Grab a jacket for the morning, shed it by lunch, and enjoy the Spurs win and UTSA's home game. Talk to you tomorrow.
